title: Israel’s gift unused; types against craving evil; testing spirits; lesser gifts
english: —the sons of Israel, though benefited so greatly, were not saved when they proved unworthy of God’s benefaction. For [[God was not well pleased with most of them >> Bible:1 Corinthians 10:5]]; they were struck down in the wilderness. And since the sinners were more and the righteous fewer, for that reason God was not well pleased with the many sinners rather than with the few righteous.

46 on [[1 Corinthians 10:6 >> Bible:1 Corinthians 10:6]]: “These things became types for us, so that we should not be desirers of evils, as they also desired.” [Origen:] He says these things have become types for us, so that we should not be desirers of evils as they desired. Those things were written typologically with a view to us, so that when we read the sins for which they suffered these things, we may keep ourselves from falling into the same desires as theirs.

47 on [[1 Corinthians 12:3 >> Bible:1 Corinthians 12:3]]: “Therefore I make known to you that no one speaking in the Spirit of God says ‘Jesus is anathema,’ and no one can say ‘Jesus is Lord’ except in the Holy Spirit.” [Origen:] There are many differences among spirits, which no one will know accurately unless he has the gift of discernment of spirits. And so that we may not too rashly either reject the spirits in those who speak or approve them, John says in the letter, [[Beloved, do not believe every spirit, but test the spirits whether they are of God; every spirit that confesses Jesus Christ come in flesh is of God, and every spirit that does not confess Jesus is not of God >> Bible:1 John 4:1-3]]. He also teaches us that when we hear people speaking we should neither assent at random nor rashly deny that what is said is from a divine spirit, but that each hearer, knowing he risks in the very act of approving or rejecting, should attend carefully neither to trust the false nor to distrust the true.

About this the apostle also adds next: [[If anyone thinks he is a prophet or spiritual, let him acknowledge that what I write is of God; but if anyone is ignorant, he is ignored >> Bible:1 Corinthians 14:37-38]]. So not only is the one who ignores the apostle’s things ignored by God, but if someone ignores while speaking by a divine spirit—and were to say that he does not speak by a divine spirit—he is ignored by God. Through these things the apostle seems to teach that there is no human who does not have another spirit in him besides the spirit of the human that is in him. Whether he is alien to the faith or belonging to it, he has a spirit belonging to him from God.

How do we who hear the divine word need to learn that no one speaking in God’s Spirit says “Jesus is anathema”? Let us see: some can be ambiguous to those who do not know the facts accurately—whether they speak by God’s Spirit or not—while they anathematize Jesus. If ever you see a Jew expounding the divine Scriptures and not contemptibly, to the many, prophetic words, you might perhaps be in doubt whether God’s Spirit is also in that one. So that you may not be pulled about over such a person—whether a holy spirit is in him or not—Paul teaches that since every Jew says Jesus is anathema, and no one speaking in God’s Spirit says Jesus is anathema, the one who claims to know the law and the prophets while anathematizing Jesus does not have God’s Spirit. There is a heresy that does not receive the one who approaches unless he anathematize Jesus. And that heresy is worthy of the name it loved; for it is the heresy of the so-called Ophites, who say unlawful things in praise of the serpent, which is cursed by God.

48 on [[1 Corinthians 12:8–10 >> Bible:1 Corinthians 12:8-10]] and [[12:27–28 >> Bible:1 Corinthians 12:27-28]]: gifts of wisdom, knowledge, faith, healings, powers, prophecy, discernments, tongues, interpretation; and God set in the church first apostles, second prophets, third teachers, then powers, then gifts of healings, helps, governances, kinds of tongues. [Origen:] There he kept the word more in order; here he comes on as if by allotment and mentions the gifts as they occur to him. Yet even so, from the second saying it rings out that the gifts worked beside the powers are lesser than the gift according to apostleship and prophecy and teaching—unless someone will grant two kinds of prophecy, so that here too the order may be kept, so that there is a—

title: Two senses of prophecy; hyperbole and love above gifts
english: —prophecy that has surpassed and a prophecy that has gone up. He will call the more catholic sort, imitating the prophecies of Isaiah and Jeremiah, second rank after the apostleship; but this last-ranked sort after the gifts already named is such as: [[if you prophesy, and an unbeliever or ungifted person comes in, he is convicted by all, examined by all, the secrets of his heart become plain, and so falling on his face he will worship God and announce that God is truly among you >> Bible:1 Corinthians 14:24-25]]. For this is not far from the working of powers and the gift of healings that happen for the amazement of those who see, so that the one prophesying may say, “You have this in your heart; from this sin you have come to the church.” This prophecy can also be later in rank than the former ones, while that more divine and greater one is second, of which he says, [[God set in the church first apostles, second prophets, third teachers >> Bible:1 Corinthians 12:28]].

To establish that two things are signified from the name “prophecy,” I set out beforehand what I said. See whether I can still show the saying more clearly: God set in the church first apostles—but not all are apostles; for if all were apostles, to whom would they minister the apostleship? Second, prophets—not all are prophets; yet according to the other prophecy, “if you all prophesy, and an unbeliever or ungifted person comes in,” it is spoken not as of an impossibility but as of a possibility that all prophesy in that way. So there are two significations from the name “prophecy.” Therefore here too the apostle’s order is kept that says first apostles, second prophets, and the rest. So much concerning the order, since the phrase “to another prophecy,” ranked last in another wording, seemed to press us.

49 on [[1 Corinthians 13:1–2 >> Bible:1 Corinthians 13:1-2]]: “And I show you a still more excellent way. If I speak with the tongues of humans and of angels, but do not have love, I have become a sounding bronze or a clanging cymbal. And if I have prophecy and know all mysteries and all knowledge, and if I have all faith so as to move mountains, but do not have love, I am nothing.” [Origen:] We ask here whether someone in this life can both have prophecy and know all the mysteries without love, and altogether whether it is given to anyone to know all mysteries; for Paul says, [[If anyone thinks he has come to know something, he does not yet know as he ought to know >> Bible:1 Corinthians 8:2]]; and again, [[we know in part and we prophesy in part; but when the perfect comes, the partial will be done away >> Bible:1 Corinthians 13:9-10]]. Saying these things about himself and the apostles like him shows that it is not possible to know all mysteries and all knowledge. How then does he speak as if it were possible to know all knowledge and understand all mysteries?

If we look at the preface of the words, in which he says, “And I show you a still more excellent way,” and understand what “excellence” (hyperbole) is, all this will be clarified. Hyperbole, then, as even the Greeks defined it, is speech that for the sake of emphasis overshoots the truth; and they use the example that some are said to be whiter than snow—not that anything can be whiter than snow, but it is said by hyperbole. And again: some horses run like wind—not that such a thing is possible, but for emphasis, so that the horses’ speed may be shown, such a thing is said of them. And in the Scripture of the Psalms it is said of the sea, [[their waves go up to the heavens and go down to the abysses >> Bible:Psalm 107:26]]—which is impossible, but said for emphasis. And in the law you will find the manner of hyperbole written where it is written, [[We saw cities great and walled up to heaven >> Bible:Deuteronomy 1:28]]. How can this be? Yet it is said hyperbolically, the speech not altogether presenting the thing signified itself but showing the greatness of the waves or the lowliness, and the greatness of the walls, or something near these.

So also here the apostle takes a hypothesis in order that the nature of gifts and the nature of love may be examined—not that it is possible for a gift, and so great a gift, to exist without love; or that it is possible in this life for someone to know all knowledge without love, or to have such faith as to move mountains; but wanting to show that if love were set in a balance—the word being spoken by hypothesis. He says, then, that one must especially zealously pursue love. Do angels—

title: Angel dialects; knowledge vs mysteries; giving and martyrdom without love; love’s praises
english: —conversing with one another—do they converse in these same tongues humans use, so that some angels would happen to be Greek, some Hebrew, others Egyptian? Or is it absurd to say this about the upper angelic ranks? Then perhaps, just as there are many dialects among humans, so also among angels? And if God grants us to be ranked from human nature into the angelic—my Lord Jesus Christ promising that [[they will be as angels and sons of God, being sons of the resurrection >> Bible:Luke 20:36]]—will we no longer use a human dialect but the angelic dialect? And just as children’s dialect differs from that of those whose voice is clear, so every human dialect is somehow a children’s dialect, while the angelic is somehow that of perfect and clear-voiced men? And perhaps there too, according to the analogy of their station, there are dialects. “If then I speak with the tongues of humans and of angels, but do not have love, I have become a sounding bronze or a clanging cymbal.” Just as sounding bronze gives an indistinct voice, and the clanging cymbal nothing clear, in the same way, without love, a tongue—even of angels among humans by hypothesis—is unclear; for nothing makes human or angelic speech clear and plain as love does; when love is absent, what is spoken is nothing.

What is the difference between knowledge and knowing the mysteries? For the apostle speaks about two things. I hold, then, that knowing about the open things is knowledge, more generic than the mysteries; for within a part of knowledge lies the science of the mysteries. But knowing about the more unspeakable and more divine things is knowing the mystery—so that there is a generic account of knowledge, yet not every grasp of knowledge is grasp of mysteries, about which it is said, [[But we speak God’s wisdom in a mystery, the hidden wisdom which God predestined before the ages for our glory >> Bible:1 Corinthians 2:7]]. When I know these things, then I have the knowledge of the mysteries. “And if I have all faith so as to move mountains”: it is written in the gospel, [[If you have faith as a mustard seed, you will say to this mountain, ‘Be taken up and thrown into the sea,’ and it will move, and nothing will be impossible for you >> Bible:Matthew 17:20]]. For the one who has faith as a mustard seed has the whole of faith.

50 on [[1 Corinthians 13:3 >> Bible:1 Corinthians 13:3]]: “And if I give away all my possessions as food, and if I hand over my body that I may boast, but do not have love, I gain nothing.” [Origen:] “If I feed people with all my goods” not because of love; “if I hand over my body that I may boast”—as if it were possible to give away goods not for love but for empty glory, and as if it were possible also to bear witness for the sake of boasting and the glory with which martyrs are glorified in the churches.

51 on [[1 Corinthians 13:4–5 >> Bible:1 Corinthians 13:4-5]]: “Love is patient, is kind; love does not envy; love does not brag, is not puffed up, does not behave indecently, does not seek its own.” [Origen:] He goes through the praises of the love that surpasses the gifts. For he had to teach both what love is and how the one who has love is. “Love is patient”: if you have patience that is a fruit of the Spirit, you have it because of love. “Is kind”: what is opposite to kindness? Wickedness. If you act wickedly against anyone, you do not have love. If you are kind and sweet toward all humans, you have love. “Love does not envy”: if there is envy in you like Cain’s toward Abel or like Joseph’s brothers toward Joseph, you do not have love. Loving and envying are fighting things. “Love does not brag”: when someone is rash, professing to know about a craft or a science or knowledge, that one is the braggart because he does not have love. “Does not behave indecently”: no one who has love does anything indecent; so if ever a brother and sister claiming to love one another according to God fall through weakness under the pretext of love, let us tell them they do not have love; for love does not behave indecently. “Does not seek its own”: no one who has love seeks his own things; for example a mother loving her son, or a father, does not seek his own as he seeks the son’s; for having love is not self-loving. If the Savior, being in the form of God and equal with God, had sought his own, he would have remained in that form; but now, wanting to save a perishing world, [[he emptied himself, taking a slave’s form >> Bible:Philippians 2:6-8]]; and being found in fashion as a human he humbled himself, becoming obedient unto—
